chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: The grandfather is apportioned equally with the brothers, whatever their number may be, even if they were one hundred thousand.

key_terms.مَا بَلَغُوا: Whatever number they reach / as many as they are
key_terms.يُقَاسِمُ: He is apportioned equally / shares equally

ai.seo_question: How is the grandfather's share calculated in relation to the brothers in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'qismah' (equal division) for the paternal grandfather when competing with brothers, establishing that the grandfather receives one share regardless of the number of brothers. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it resolves the debate between the 'dhawu al-furud' (fixed share holders) and 'dhawu al-asabah' (residuary heirs) schools, affirming the grandfather's status as a primary heir alongside brothers. The narration underscores the egalitarian nature of this specific inheritance tier, ensuring the grandfather's share is not diluted by the quantity of siblings.
